basic_information.short_title: Bangsamoro Agriculture and Fisheries Training Institute Act
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE BANGSAMORO AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES TRAINING INSTITUTE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in a newspaper of general circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Creates a training institute for the region's farmers and fisherfolk — technical courses, extension services, technology transfer and halal industry development — with a training officer posted in every province.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: To promote agriculture and fisheries as a means of alleviating poverty and ensuring food sufficiency, by giving farmers and fisherfolk access to science and technology training and modern techniques.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: A Bangsamoro Agriculture and Fisheries Training Institute leads technical training and the regional extension agenda, accredits private extension providers, supports LGU extension workers, and prioritises halal industry development in every training module.
who_will_be_affected: Farmers and fisherfolk across the region
LGU extension workers, who get capability-building and technical assistance
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2024 — 15 days after publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. There is an institute whose job is training farmers and fisherfolk — with a training officer in every province and the Special Geographic Areas, and halal standards built into every module.
in_practice: The Bangsamoro Agriculture and Fisheries Training Institute (BAFTI), attached to the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform
Leads technical training and short courses, and formulates the regional Agriculture and Fisheries Extension agenda and budget
A BAFTI Training Officer stationed in each island and mainland province and in the Special Geographic Areas, to reach far-flung areas
Training needs assessments conducted with the ministry and the LGU, so training is correct, culturally appropriate and relevant
Information materials delivered in the language most appropriate to the end-user
Learning sites identified where successful farmers share their technologies on their own farms
An accreditation system for private entities providing extension services
Halal industry development prioritised, with halal standards and incentives in all training modules

for_specific_groups.Farmers and fisherfolk: You are the intended end-users — training, technology transfer, post-harvest handling, marketing and financing knowledge, delivered in your own language.
for_specific_groups.Cooperatives: Farmers' and fisherfolks' cooperatives are named the cornerstone of training development and dissemination, in partnership with the Cooperative and Social Enterprise Authority.
for_specific_groups.LGU extension workers: The Institute assists the local extension system with capability-building, technical assistance, training, facilities and research-based programmes.
for_specific_groups.Halal businesses: Halal food, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, tourism, logistics, Islamic financing, modest fashion and related markets are all within the act's definition of the halal industry.
for_specific_groups.Communities in the Special Geographic Ar: A training officer is to be stationed there as well as in the provinces.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The whole BARMM, including the island provinces and the Special Geographic Areas.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Through training programmes, extension services and learning sites.
what_you_can_do: Ask your provincial BAFTI Training Officer about training programmes and needs assessments
Ask about accreditation if you provide extension services privately
Ask about halal certification support for food businesses
watch_out_for: Only one institute is established at first; further sites depend on an assessment 2 years after the first one opens.
₱10 million is a modest start for a region-wide training mandate.
The Institute trains and coordinates; it does not provide subsidies, credit or inputs.

key_terms_explained.Extension services: Training, information and support delivered to farmers and fisherfolk to improve their technical, business and social capabilities — including post-harvest training and market analysis.
key_terms_explained.BAFTI Training Officer: The focal person in each province and Special Geographic Area, responsible for training needs assessment, designing and delivering programmes, and evaluating them.
key_terms_explained.Halal industry: Defined broadly by the act — halal food, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, Muslim-friendly tourism, logistics, Islamic financing, modest fashion, media and recreation.
key_terms_explained.Ladderized training: Courses that build on each other so a learner can progress step by step.
key_terms_explained.SUCs: State Universities and Colleges, partners in developing training modules.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Muharram 11, 1446 / 17 July 2024, approved by the Chief Minister on 19 August 2024.

benefits.headline: Technical training, extension support and halal development for the region's farmers and fisherfolk.

direct_benefits.benefit: Technical training and short courses in agriculture and fisheries
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Through BAFTI and its provincial training officers

direct_benefits.benefit: Training in your own language, based on a needs assessment for your area
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Sections 9 requires culturally appropriate materials in the appropriate language

direct_benefits.benefit: Learning sites on successful farmers' own farms
Support for halal certification in the food industry

indirect_benefits: Ladderized agriculture and fisheries short courses with technical education
limitations: One institute initially; expansion depends on a two-year assessment.
It trains and coordinates rather than financing production.

for_citizens: None. The act imposes no duty on farmers or fisherfolk.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.oversight: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform, to which BAFTI is attached and to whose Minister the Executive Director reports directly
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A rice farmer in a far-flung municipality wants post-harvest training. A BAFTI Training Officer is to be stationed in each province and the Special Geographic Areas precisely to reach areas like theirs.
A fisherfolk cooperative wants help with marketing and financing. Section 4(g) covers benchmarking, production, harvesting, storage, processing, marketing and financing for cooperative members.

A small food producer wants halal certification. Section 10 requires BAFTI to support policies for halal certification in the food industry and to include halal standards and incentives in all training modules.
A successful farmer is willing to host demonstrations. Section 4(j) has BAFTI identify learning sites where farmers share technologies on their own farms.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Bangsamoro Agriculture and Fisheries Training Institute Act”.

Section 2 — Policy: promote agriculture and fisheries to alleviate poverty and ensure food sufficiency; give priority to science and technology training and innovation for all Bangsamoro farmers and fisherfolk; and develop an extensive information campaign disseminating modern techniques, innovations and knowledge, toward enhanced production, competitiveness and strengthened extension institutions.

Section 3 — Defines agricultural and fisheries extension services, agriculture, fisheries, the BAFTI Training Officer, halal food, and the halal industry — the last covering halal food, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, Muslim-friendly tourism, logistics and supply chain, Islamic financing, training standards, modest fashion, media and recreation, in strict compliance with Shari'ah including as expressed by the Bangsamoro Darul Ifta'.

Section 4 — BAFTI leads technical training and short courses; formulates the regional Agriculture and Fisheries Extension agenda and budget; prepares an integrated plan for publicly funded training; issues guidelines with the agriculture ministry for planning, implementing, monitoring and evaluating extension programmes and accrediting extension services; assists the LGU extension system with capability-building, technical assistance and training; establishes technology transfer mechanisms to farmers and fisherfolk; supports all extension workers with knowledge of benchmarking, production, harvesting, storage, processing, marketing and financing; accredits private extension providers; links small farmers with market stakeholders; identifies learning sites on successful farmers' own farms; and promotes innovation and diversification.

Section 5 — BAFTI is established in the administrative capital, headed by an Executive Director holding a master's degree in Agriculture or Fisheries with 5 years' supervisory or management experience and Career Service Professional Eligibility or its equivalent. 2 years after the first institute is established there shall be an overall assessment of its operations and programmes, which determines subsequent establishments in the island and mainland provinces including a site in the Special Geographic Area. BAFTI and its satellite offices are attached to the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform, with the Executive Director reporting directly to the Minister.

Sections 6–8 — Training Officers are stationed in the island and mainland provinces and the Special Geographic Area; farmers' and fisherfolks' cooperatives are the cornerstone of training development in partnership with the Cooperative and Social Enterprise Authority; and BAFTI gives priority to research, keeping current with modern trends including machinery, with training modules developed with State Universities and Colleges.

Section 9 — BAFTI, with the agriculture ministry and the concerned LGU, conducts a Training Needs Assessment so that training is correct, culturally appropriate and relevant, and delivers information, education and communication materials in the language most appropriate to the end-user.

Section 10 — BAFTI prioritises development of the halal industry, includes halal standards and incentives in all training modules, and supports policies for halal certification in the food industry to protect Bangsamoro consumers.

Sections 11–13 — Agriculture and fisheries short courses including long-term ladderized training with technical education; coordination with ministries, agencies and local and international organisations to avoid duplication; and active encouragement of private sector participation and public-private partnerships.

Section 14 — An initial ₱10,000,000 is appropriated, with such sums as needed thereafter in the annual General Appropriations Act, and continuous allocation for BAFTI's infrastructure once the first institute is established.
Section 15 — Implementing rules within 90 days from the agriculture ministry, with the finance minister and the Chairperson of the Committee on Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform.
Section 18 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in a newspaper of general circulation.

citizen_questions.q: What does the Institute actually offer?
citizen_questions.a: Technical training and short courses in agriculture and fisheries, extension services, technology transfer, and support for cooperatives — with a training officer in each province and the Special Geographic Areas.

citizen_questions.q: Will training be in my language?
citizen_questions.a: Section 9 requires culturally appropriate information, education and communication materials in the language most appropriate to the end-user, based on a training needs assessment for your area.
Yes. Section 10 requires BAFTI to prioritise halal industry development, include halal standards and incentives in all training modules, and support halal certification policies in the food industry.

citizen_questions.q: How many institutes will there be?
citizen_questions.a: One at first, in the administrative capital. 2 years after it opens, an overall assessment determines where further institutes are established across the island and mainland provinces, including a site in the Special Geographic Area.
₱10 million initially, with further sums in the annual budget and continuing allocation for infrastructure.
